proven: Ambient text, distillation batches, language aggregates and clip bytes exclude expired captures without relying on the cleanup worker
The exact 48-hour boundary is expired, including after reopening the SQLite store
New UUID capture IDs survive restart and differ between databases even when SQLite row IDs coincide
New capture expiry is persisted; extending configuration later or a future capture timestamp cannot extend its original deadline
Invalid capture timestamps and invalid/over-48-hour retention settings are rejected
Legacy schema migration preserves existing metadata and leaves newly introduced capture IDs and expiry fields null rather than fabricating them
Removing expired rows and queuing their known clip paths happen in one owned SQLite transaction
An unlink failure leaves a durable retry entry that survives restart and ignores the misleading fresh mtime of a known expired clip
Cancellation during a transaction or native unlink cannot abandon its actual outcome or forget the deletion intent
A clip that expires during disk read is not returned
The configured archive boundary prevents reading or deleting an outside file; failed cleanup remains reported
Cancelled archive writes wait actual native completion and route late or partial bytes through the durable discard callback
The connected transcriber cannot recreate a purged source through a late archive pointer
Purge runs at startup, schedules the earliest persisted deadline and wakes for a newly earlier capture instead of waiting the full hourly audit interval
The factory wires archive discard to the store and the source-free artifact exercises real temporary SQLite retention and byte cleanup

implementation.clock: Injected epoch clock; persisted expiry is the capture-start/insertion minimum plus the initial retention
